question.text: When two competing open offers are running simultaneously under the SEBI (SAST) Regulations, which of the following statements is correct?

answer.text: Shareholders who have tendered shares in acceptance of one offer may withdraw that acceptance during the tendering period and switch to the other offer
Shareholders can tender the same shares to both offers simultaneously and receive consideration from both acquirers
Tendering timelines for the competing offers are aligned and acquirers may revise the terms of their offers upward before the tendering period commences
SEBI must first declare one of the offers as the preferred offer before shareholders may tender any shares

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the workbook, competing offers run on aligned timelines so that the tendering period for the first offer and the competing offer coincide. Each acquirer may revise the terms of its offer upward (price and/or size) up to 1 working day before the tendering period commences. Shareholders who tender their shares in acceptance of an open offer are NOT entitled to withdraw such acceptance during the tendering period. The Trap: The intuitive notion that shareholders can "switch" between competing offers during the tendering window is incorrect. The competing-offer regime gives shareholders the benefit of price revisions by the acquirers themselves; once they have tendered, the acceptance is irrevocable for the duration of the tendering period. Note: Because revisions to terms must be made before the tendering period commences, shareholders see the final competing prices when they decide whether and to whom to tender.
